title: Rounded rectangular prism (2 parts)
spec:
Start by constructing a rounded rectangular prism base. First, create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw the first two-dimensional sketch on the first face. This involves creating a loop with four arcs and four lines. The first arc starts at coordinates (0.0, 0.0045), has a midpoint at (0.0013, 0.0013), and ends at (0.0045, 0.0). The first line starts at (0.0045, 0.0) and ends at (0.0224, 0.0). The second arc starts at (0.0224, 0.0), has a midpoint at (0.0256, 0.0013), and ends at (0.0269, 0.0045). The second line starts at (0.0269, 0.0045) and ends at (0.0269, 0.0224). The third arc starts at (0.0269, 0.0224), has a midpoint at (0.0256, 0.0256), and ends at (0.0224, 0.0269). The third line starts at (0.0224, 0.0269) and ends at (0.0045, 0.0269). The fourth arc starts at (0.0045, 0.0269), has a midpoint at (0.0013, 0.0256), and ends at (0.0, 0.0224). The fourth line starts at (0.0, 0.0224) and ends at (0.0, 0.0045). Apply a scale factor of 0.0269 to the sketch. Rotate the sketch using Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] and translate it using a translation vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Extrude the sketch 0.75 units along the normal direction without extruding in the opposite direction. The final part will be a cylindrical object with a flat top and bottom, where the top surface is slightly wider than the bottom, with dimensions of length 0.0269, width 0.0269, and height 0.75.

Next, construct a triangular section cut out. Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to [90.0, 0.0, -90.0] and a translation vector set to [0.0, 0.0269, 0.7035]. Draw the first two-dimensional sketch on the first face, which consists of a loop with three lines. The first line starts at (0.0, 0.0465) and ends at (0.0045, 0.0388). The second line starts at (0.0045, 0.0388) and ends at (0.0045, 0.0465). The third line starts at (0.0045, 0.0465) and ends at (0.0, 0.0465). On the second face, draw another loop with four lines. The first line starts at (0.0045, 0.0388) and ends at (0.0224, 0.0078). The second line starts at (0.0224, 0.0078) and ends at (0.0224, 0.0465). The third line starts at (0.0224, 0.0465) and ends at (0.0045, 0.0465). The fourth line starts at (0.0045, 0.0465) and ends at (0.0045, 0.0388). On the third face, draw another loop with four lines. The first line starts at (0.0224, 0.0078) and ends at (0.0269, 0.0). The second line starts at (0.0269, 0.0) and ends at (0.0269, 0.0465). The third line starts at (0.0269, 0.0465) and ends at (0.0224, 0.0465). The fourth line starts at (0.0224, 0.0465) and ends at (0.0224, 0.0078). Apply a scale factor of 0.0465 to the sketch. Rotate the sketch using Euler angles [90.0, 0.0, -90.0] and translate it using a translation vector [0.0, 0.0269, 0.7035]. Do not extrude in the normal direction; instead, extrude the sketch 0.0269 units in the opposite direction of the normal. The final part will be a cube with a triangular section cut out from one of its faces, with dimensions of length 0.0269, width 0.0465, and height 0.0269.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Part 1: Create the base shape (rectangular prism with rounded corners)
base_shape = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .moveTo(0.0, 0.0045)
    .threePointArc((0.0013, 0.0013), (0.0045, 0.0))
    .lineTo(0.0224, 0.0)
    .threePointArc((0.0256, 0.0013), (0.0269, 0.0045))
    .lineTo(0.0269, 0.0224)
    .threePointArc((0.0256, 0.0256), (0.0224, 0.0269))
    .lineTo(0.0045, 0.0269)
    .threePointArc((0.0013, 0.0256), (0.0, 0.0224))
    .lineTo(0.0, 0.0045)
    .close()
    .extrude(0.75)
)

# Part 2: Create the cutting shape (triangular section)
cut_shape = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .moveTo(0.0, 0.0465)
    .lineTo(0.0045, 0.0388)
    .lineTo(0.0224, 0.0078)
    .lineTo(0.0269, 0.0)
    .lineTo(0.0269, 0.0465)
    .lineTo(0.0045, 0.0465)
    .close()
    .extrude(-0.0269)
)

# Translate the cutting shape to the correct position
cut_shape = cut_shape.translate((0.0, 0.0269, 0.7035))

# Perform the cut operation
r = base_shape.cut(cut_shape)

# Display the final result
